invariants.requirement: Snapshot IDs are unsigned, monotonic, and never reused.
Immutable object identity is snapshot, ordinal, and an explicit type.
Distributed filesystem objects use Raft-allocated snapshot origins and route directly by origin.
invariants.gap: Live handoff uses path-free graph roots, but filesystem repositories still allocate local origins and stopped/dehydrated filesystem publication still uses cold packs.

invariants.requirement: Sealed objects and graph metadata never change in place.
Every immutable object has exactly one authoritative reference ledger.
invariants.gap: Flattened filesystem cold packs are not represented by the origin ledger.

invariants.requirement: Volatile origin authority transitions only from its provider node to shared storage.
invariants.gap: Distributed filesystem storage still uses generation manifests outside this transition.

invariants.requirement: Each immutable parent edge contributes exactly one child reference independent of root count.
A zero authoritative reference count is sufficient to reclaim an immutable object.
invariants.gap: Filesystem cold-pack reclamation still uses manifest tracing and grace-based collection.

invariants.requirement: Open-unlinked, executable, mapped, and FUSE-held objects remain explicit roots until last use.
Snapshot publication cannot mutate branch lifecycle or placement.
Publication is restartable, idempotent, generation-fenced, and cancelable by removal.
invariants.gap: Graph memory publication meets the invariant; legacy filesystem cold-pack publication must be converted.

invariants.requirement: A branch executes only under its committed placement generation and a valid node lease.
Bulk data uses structural validation and normal reads do not require TTC checksums.
Fork and seal are O(1) in resident pages and recursive file count.
invariants.gap: Independent page-count, file-count, directory-width, and fork-depth distributions remain to be recorded.

invariants.requirement: Standalone TTC uses no Raft, shared packs, cache tier, or lazy image materialization.
A new-format root cannot execute any legacy storage fallback.
invariants.gap: Startup rejection is covered, but the required strict runtime test switch has not been added.
